title: A consuming repo cannot ask "was this dist built from the tree I pin?" — the content stamp already exists, covers only the AMPLIFIERS list, and is not readable across the repo boundary
body:
Filed by the `repo:cloud` execution seat (seat post #6026, session `session_01Gp1JypWKsxjpn1wb2JdqAY`) as the framework-side residue of **cloud#2026**, which landed the consumer half. ⛔ Ungraded and unrouted on purpose — `domain:*`, type and priority are triage's. Expected `domain:devx`.

⚠️ **The dev that surfaced this framed it as "stamp the source SHA into the build output". That framing is wrong and I am not filing it** — the mechanism already exists and is better than a SHA. What is actually missing is coverage and cross-repo readability. Grounded below rather than asserted.

## The consumer-side problem, already measured

cloud links `@objectstack/*` packages by `link:` into a sibling `objectstack` checkout — **184 such specifiers**, measured on cloud `main`. When that checkout's `dist/` was built from a different tree than the one cloud pins, the failure surfaces as a `TS2305` naming an import nobody touched:

```
src/organizations-plugin.ts(5,10): error TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/plugin-auth"'
  has no exported member 'isDefaultOrganizationBootstrapTrigger'
```

The symbol exists at the pin. The sibling's `plugin-auth/dist/index.d.ts` was built Aug 29; its `src/index.ts` is Sep 6.

cloud#2026 (PR objectstack-ai/cloud#2042) closed the half cloud can close: its preflight now compares each linked sibling's `git rev-parse HEAD` against cloud's pin file, resolving the sibling through `node_modules` rather than through the `link:` specifier.

⛔ **That check is HEAD-based, and its own docblock records why that is not enough:** a sibling sitting **exactly on the pin** whose `dist/` was built from an older commit produces the identical `TS2305`, and a HEAD comparison stays silent through it. Cloud cannot close that half, because **the build output carries no record of the tree it came from** — and reaching for `dist/` vs `src/` mtimes is the manufactured confidence this whole family of cards is about.

## What already exists here — read before designing anything

`scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs` implements exactly the right primitive, and its docblock is explicit about the properties:

- **a build-time content stamp, never mtime** (`--stamp`, criterion recorded against #5864) — *"immune to clock skew, NFS timestamps, `touch` — because none of them change file bytes"*;
- **written by the package's OWN build script as its last step** (`node ../../scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs --stamp`), so the fact recorded is *"this dist was produced by this build"*;
- **extending it is cheap and the file says so**: *"Adding the next amplifier is two lines: its path in `AMPLIFIERS`, and `--stamp`"*, with a coverage gate — a listed package whose build does not stamp fails, and `--stamp` from an unlisted package exits 1.

Two limits it already records, both load-bearing here:

1. *"freshness can only be asserted for a package whose build writes the stamp, and rolling that line into 60+ build scripts is a change to [scope]"* — i.e. the `AMPLIFIERS` list is deliberately partial.
2. The stamp is written **unconditionally**, including when the build short-circuited and produced nothing new. `packages/spec/scripts/lib/dist-freshness.ts` rejected a stamp-based guard for its own purpose on exactly this ground, while explicitly recording that *"the stamp's own strength — content, not mtime — is real"*.

⇒ **The gap is not "no mechanism". It is (a) the packages cloud links are not in `AMPLIFIERS`, and (b) nothing exposes the stamp for a reader outside this repository.**

## The ask

Not a design; the readings above should decide it. Two candidate shapes:

- **Extend coverage** — add the packages a downstream repo actually links (`plugin-auth`, `core`, `organizations`, and the rest of cloud's 184-specifier closure) to `AMPLIFIERS`. Cheap per the file's own "two lines", but it multiplies the unconditional-stamp weakness across more packages, so limit 2 should be settled first or the stamp will assert freshness it does not have.
- **Expose the stamp across the boundary** — a documented, stable location and format a consuming repo may read, so cloud's preflight can ask *"was this `dist/` produced from the tree I pin?"* instead of the weaker *"is HEAD on the pin?"*. This is the half cloud cannot build for itself.

⚠️ Whoever takes it should decide whether limit 2 (unconditional stamping) has to be fixed **first**. A stamp that a consumer trusts is a stronger contract than a stamp that only gates a local dev prereq, and `dist-freshness.ts` already declined to rely on it in its current form.

## Family — this is not a fresh area

Adjacent open cards, all on dist-staleness detection: **#16241** (the bundle-freshness refusal names one cause for three distinguishable states) · **#16175** (`schemaTreeIsStale` / `bundlesAreStale` carry the mtime false refusal #14985 fixed for `distIsStale`) · **#15822** (`newestSourceMtime` still walks gitignored paths). Closed ancestors: **#14985** (mtime → content hash for `distIsStale`) · **#7122** (a stale dist launders a phantom breaking removal into the committed baseline) · **#5864** (the content-not-mtime criterion).

⇒ Triage should consider whether this belongs **folded into that family** rather than standing alone — it is the same criterion (content, not mtime) asked from one repo further out. This card exists because the cross-repo reader is a consumer none of those cards has.

## Re-check

```
git grep -n "AMPLIFIERS" -- scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs
git grep -n "stamp" -- packages/spec/scripts/lib/dist-freshness.ts    # the recorded refusal to rely on it
```
Consumer side: `scripts/preflight-workspace-dist.mjs` in `objectstack-ai/cloud` after PR #2042, function `pinFreshness` — its doc states the residual limit this card is about.

Refs: cloud#2026 · objectstack-ai/cloud PR #2042 · #14985 · #7122 · #5864 · #16241 · #16175
